text:
mike: Heads-up — reopening the min on-demand floor convo. We've been running 10% in us-west for the last quarter and jitter/cold-starts on tail latency are creeping up. Can we talk sustainable floor + ephemeral burst sizing?

ana: Agree. Costs are fine, but some RL workloads hit 95th percentile spikes when spot evicts. We need a better interruption-handling plan, not just raise the floor.

li: For context, recent 2-week metrics: spot interruption rate in us-west-2 jumped to ~7.8% (vs 3% baseline in us-east-1). Pod churn => KV cache misses => +30ms p50 and +180ms p95 for long-context models.

devon: Proposal idea: keep a low steady min_on_demand (10-15%) globally, but enable a regional boost when interruption_rate > 5% for 24h. Also attach a tiny hot-warm burst pool (ephemeral nodes) sized to absorb 20% of normal peak.

sam: Question: how do we manage cost/billing attribution when we temporarily spin up regional boosts? We need clear credits to product teams or will hit cost surprises.

ana: We can gate regional boosts behind budget thresholds per org + automated rollback. Also suggest autoscaling cooldowns to avoid flip-flop.

mike: Sketch of the behavior we want:
- steady min_on_demand floor (0.12 global default)
- ephemeral burst floor that can ramp up to X% of fleet for 2h windows
- region-aware override when preemptible_rate > threshold
- graceful eviction plan: route inflight to on-demand variant + KV cache warm-up flags

li: Sample policy YAML (concept):

```yaml
policy_name: sustainable-floor-v1
min_on_demand: 0.12   # fraction of total GPU capacity
burst_pool_max: 0.20  # fraction for ephemeral burst nodes
region_override:
  enabled: true
  threshold: 0.05   # interruption rate to trigger override
  max_boost: 0.15
cooldowns:
  scale_up: 60s
  scale_down: 15m
interruption_handling:
  fallback_model: variant-small
  route_grace_period: 30s
  kv_preload: true
```

devon: That looks reasonable. For route_grace_period, 30s is fine for short queries but not for long-streaming responses. Maybe differentiate by request_size or streaming flag. Marking as TODO.

ops-bot: Deploy-check: canary 5% rollout to us-west-2 routing changes scheduled if we still want to test before org-level rollout.

sam: Dev teams asking for SLA guarantees — if we do dynamic region boosts, we should publish expected latency delta and cost delta so they can opt-in.

ana: Also consider a fallback routing policy that prefers nearby regions but allows cross-region fallbacks if latency delta < 50ms. Helps absorb capacity shortages without huge cost.

li: Ops note: network egress and inter-region KV sync is the real cost here. If we move traffic cross-region for fallbacks we need to account for egress and cache warmups. Add that to the cost model.

mike: Action items:
- li: run a 2-week simulation of regional override behavior with current interruption traces, output expected p95 and cost deltas (due Fri)
- ana: draft org-level budget guardrails and rollback rules (Mon)
- devon: prototype burst pool autoscaler with cooldown heuristics (start PoC)
- sam: prepare a short opt-in SLA doc describing tradeoffs for product teams

devon: One more thought — add a cheap checkpointing mechanism to KV cache so on-demand handoffs have faster warmups. Could be a small disk-backed snapshot per model shard.

mike: Love it. Keep the thread tight. If the sim looks good we'll canary the policy in us-west and us-east small groups. :rocket: 

ops-bot: Note — monitoring alert will auto-create an incident channel if regional interruption_rate > 0.12 for 6h.

li: I'll post the sim results and sample graphs here when ready.

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
